## What determines your PCI compliance cost: merchant level


PCI DSS cost depends first on your merchant level, set by annual card transaction volume. The level decides whether you self-assess or pay for a full on-site assessment:


Level Transaction volume What is required


Level 1 6M+ transactions a year Annual Report on Compliance (ROC) by a QSA, quarterly ASV scans


Level 2 1M to 6M SAQ or ROC, quarterly ASV scans


Level 3 20K to 1M e-commerce SAQ, quarterly ASV scans


Level 4 Under 20K e-commerce SAQ, scans as required by your acquirer


A self-assessment questionnaire (SAQ) is far cheaper than a Qualified Security Assessor (QSA) audit, so your level is the single biggest cost driver.

## ✨ Where cardholder data discovery saves the most


The biggest cost lever in PCI is scope: every system that stores, processes, or transmits card data must be assessed. Most teams do not know everywhere card data has leaked, so they over-scope and over-pay. Finding and minimizing cardholder data (PCI DSS Requirement 12.5.2) shrinks the assessment and the bill.


Strac Comply finds cardholder data automatically, so you scope tightly and pay less.

## PCI compliance cost checklist


- Confirm your merchant level and whether you need a SAQ or a ROC.
- Find all cardholder data and reduce scope before you assess.
- Budget for quarterly ASV scans and an annual penetration test.
- Automate evidence so you are audit-ready year-round.
- Segment your network to keep systems out of scope.


## How to lower your PCI compliance cost


- Reduce your cardholder data footprint first; less data in scope means a smaller, cheaper assessment.
- Automate data discovery so you are not paying a consultant to find cardholder data by hand.
- Confirm your merchant level before buying a QSA audit you may not need.
- Keep evidence continuous so you are audit-ready instead of scrambling each year.

## 🌶️ Spicy FAQs: PCI compliance cost


### What is the cheapest way to become PCI compliant?


Reduce scope. The fewer systems that touch cardholder data, the smaller your assessment. Qualifying for a self-assessment questionnaire instead of a QSA audit, and discovering and minimizing where card data lives, are the biggest levers. Strac Comply automates the data discovery that drives scope.


### Does PCI compliance require a QSA?


Only Level 1 merchants (6 million-plus transactions a year) need a Qualified Security Assessor to produce a Report on Compliance. Smaller merchants usually complete a self-assessment questionnaire, which is far cheaper.


### Is PCI compliance a one-time or annual cost?


Annual. You validate every year with a SAQ or ROC, run quarterly ASV scans, and typically a yearly penetration test. Automating evidence and keeping scope small keeps the recurring number down.
